Акромиально-ключичный сустав соединяет л: The acromioclavicular joint (ACJ) links the lateral clavicle and the acromion of the scapula, which projects anteriorly; it provides stability and motion to the shoulder complex and is a commonly injured joint, with injuries ranging from sprains to frank tears. The coracoclavicular ligament (CCL) is the primary support structure of the ACJ, and stability comes from the coordinated action of two ligaments. The ACJ is a synovial planar joint.
Диартроз, плоский синовиальный сустав с: A diarthrodial, planar synovial joint that permits mainly gliding motion; it is part of the scapulothoracic linkage, contributing to scapular mobility and to shoulder abduction and flexion, and it transmits force from the upper limb to the axial skeleton. The joint is enclosed by a fibrous capsule and lined by synovial membrane, an intra-articular fibrocartilaginous disk lies between the bony surfaces, and the articular surfaces are covered by fibrocartilage, not hyaline cartilage.
Сустав стабилизируют три связки: акромиа: Three ligaments stabilize the ACJ: the acromioclavicular ligament, the CCL complex and the coracoacromial ligament. The acromioclavicular ligament has superior, inferior, anterior and posterior components (the superior and posterior parts are strongest), and its primary role is horizontal stability.
Клювовидно-ключичная связка — главный вн: The coracoclavicular ligament (CCL) is the primary extrinsic stabilizer of the ACJ; it runs from the coracoid process to the inferior surface of the lateral one-third of the clavicle and is composed of the conoid and trapezoid ligaments, which insert on the posteromedial and anterolateral undersurface of the distal clavicle, respectively. The trapezoid ligament inserts about 3 cm from the distal clavicle, lies anterolateral to the conoid, is quadrilateral, thinner than the conoid and courses anterolaterally. The conoid ligament inserts about 4.5 cm from the distal clavicle at the conoid tubercle (posteromedial to the trapezoid tubercle), is conical (broad clavicular end, narrow coracoid end), courses posteromedially toward the root of the coracoid and is near-vertical. Both ligaments join at the coracoid attachment and diverge toward the clavicle, and a bursa often separates them. The CCL does not cross the ACJ directly; it maintains the spatial relationship between clavicle and acromion.
Два основных источника: ветви надлопаточ: Two main arterial sources supply the ACJ: branches of the suprascapular artery (from the subclavian artery) and branches of the thoracoacromial artery (from the axillary artery). The CCL receives its main supply from the suprascapular artery (originating from the subclavian artery via the thyrocervical trunk) and the thoracoacromial branch (from the axillary artery). Venous drainage from the CCL region is through the suprascapular vein, which drains toward the external jugular vein. Lymph drains to the axillary and cervical lymphatic basins.
По закону Хилтона суставы получают суста: Per Hilton's law, joints receive articular branches from nerves that supply the muscles acting across them. The ACJ is innervated by articular branches of the suprascapular, axillary and lateral pectoral nerves, all from the brachial plexus; cutaneous sensation is supplied by a sensory branch of the suprascapular nerve, which runs superiorly to the supraspinatus toward the ACJ. ACJ pain may be referred to the neck, trapezius, lateral deltoid and shoulder. The CCL region receives articular branches from the suprascapular, axillary and lateral pectoral nerves.
Клювовидно-ключичная связка поддерживает: The CCL helps support the coracoclavicular articulation during complex shoulder movements and limits separation between scapula and clavicle. Muscles named as primarily involved in movement and stabilization of these structures are the serratus anterior, trapezius, teres major, rhomboid major, rhomboid minor and long head of triceps brachii; their scapular attachments help stabilize the coracoclavicular complex and restrict excessive motion. The pectoralis minor tendon crosses the fascial arch formed by the medial CCL at the coracoid process.
Исследование 2021 г. выявило замещение с: A 2021 study reported ligament replacement by a coracoclavicular bone bridge in 9% of 2,724 subjects, more often in African American individuals and women. Reported coracoclavicular joint (CCJ) prevalence varies widely; a 2023 study of a French population compared with medieval skeletal remains found 0.82%. A cadaveric study of 24 CCL specimens identified three conoid ligament variants among 18 conoid ligaments: 9 attached to the root of the coracoid process, 6 were confluent with the superior transverse scapular ligament and 3 had a distinct fascicle from the inferior conoid attachment inserting on the lateral trapezoid ligament.
Повреждения акромиально-ключичного суста: ACJ injuries are common, most often sprains, and account for more than 40% of shoulder injuries. Mechanisms include direct trauma or lateral shoulder impact causing axial loading, motor vehicle collisions, sports injuries, accidental trauma and falls onto an outstretched hand or elbow; ACJ dislocation is distinct from glenohumeral "shoulder dislocation." Presentation: localized ACJ pain after a relevant mechanism, possibly radiating to the shoulder or neck and worsened by arm use, with swelling, ecchymosis, localized tenderness, reduced active and passive range of motion and visible deformity in dislocation; anteroposterior and superoinferior mobility are assessed for laxity, together with the whole clavicle and shoulder and a complete neurovascular exam.
Тесты: тест приведения (перекрёстный) —: Special tests: the adduction (cross-arm) test is the most sensitive maneuver (pain at the ACJ is positive); the shear test applies opposing anterior and posterior forces on the clavicle and scapula; the Paxinos (one-handed shear) test places the thumb on the posterior acromion and fingers on the midclavicle, then compresses the two points. Imaging: anteroposterior, lateral and axillary radiographs; the Zanca view (AP view with 10° cephalic tilt centered on the ACJ) gives the most accurate ACJ assessment when uncertainty persists; grade I sprains typically show normal radiographs, and ultrasound or MRI may be used when uncertainty persists.
Классификация Роквуда: I — растяжение ак: Rockwood classification: grade I, AC ligament sprain with CCL intact and no radiographic abnormality; grade II, AC ligament torn and CCL sprained, with the clavicle elevated but not above the acromion border or less than 25% widening of the coracoclavicular interspace; grade III, AC ligament and CCL torn, with the clavicle above the acromion border or 25% to 100% widening of the interspace; grade IV, AC ligament and CCL torn with posterior displacement of the distal clavicle into the trapezius; grade V, AC ligament and CCL torn with superior displacement of the distal clavicle greater than 25 mm; grade VI, AC ligament and CCL torn with inferolateral displacement to a subacromial or subcoracoid position, posterior to the coracobrachialis or biceps tendon.
Прогноз в целом благоприятный. I–II степ: The prognosis is generally favorable. Grades I and II are managed conservatively (rest, sling, ice, anti-inflammatories, physical therapy, gradual return to activity); grade III management is controversial, with the choice depending on occupation, functional demands, goals and orthopedic consultation; grades IV to VI are rare and usually require surgery because of instability and risk of associated injuries, and surgical cases have longer recovery and higher complication rates. Complications: persistent pain is the most common (about 30% to 50% of cases); primary and secondary osteoarthritis are common and increase with age (overuse, chronic degeneration, prior trauma), secondary osteoarthritis causes narrowing of the articular disc and worsening cartilage degeneration, and progression can cause osteophytes, subacromial impingement and compression of nearby structures.
Септический артрит акромиально-ключичног: Septic arthritis of the ACJ can cause significant morbidity and mortality and is often confused with glenohumeral septic arthritis because the presentations overlap; pain and erythema over the ACJ are characteristic. It is rare and mainly affects immunocompromised people and men in their 5th and 6th decades, usually from hematogenous spread; highly vascular joints are more susceptible, and the ACJ is less often affected because of its limited vascularity and small size. A case was reported in a 69-year-old man with Klinefelter syndrome. Metabolic syndrome (obesity, hypercholesterolemia, hypertension, impaired glucose tolerance) is associated with a higher risk of ACJ pathology. Organisms named: Staphylococcus aureus, Cryptococcus neoformans and Haemophilus influenzae. Osteomyelitis can follow surgical reconstruction, with poor hygiene and nonadherence to wound care as possible risk factors. Management usually involves IV antibiotics and often surgical exploration.
Остеоартроз клювовидно-ключичного сустав: Coracoclavicular joint (CCJ) osteoarthritis: the CCJ is rare and degeneration of the CCL within it is rarer; it may cause shoulder pain and diagnosis is often delayed because clinicians may not consider it. Useful imaging is standing radiographs and dynamic MRI, and it can be distinguished from subcoracoid impingement with a local anesthetic injection. Nonoperative treatment is anti-inflammatories, physiotherapy and corticosteroid injections, and surgical excision is for cases that do not respond to conservative care. The CCJ may limit shoulder movement, cause pain and in some people worsen thoracic outlet syndrome.
Глотка — срединный воронкообразный прово: The pharynx is a midline, funnel-shaped conducting structure in the neck, shared by the gastrointestinal tract and the respiratory system; its wider upper end sits just below the base of the skull and its narrower lower end is at the level of C6, where the esophagus (posteriorly) and larynx (anteriorly) begin. Its muscular-membranous structure supports swallowing, air conduction and voice production.
Три отдела сверху вниз: носоглотка — поз: The pharynx has three regions, from superior to inferior: the nasopharynx behind the choanae, which carries only respiratory traffic as air passes from the nasal cavities; the oropharynx behind the oral cavity, which moves the food bolus downward; and the laryngopharynx behind the laryngeal inlet, which passes food into the esophagus.
На боковой стенке носоглотки лежат два о: Two auditory (pharyngotympanic/Eustachian) tube openings lie on the lateral wall of the nasopharynx, each surrounded by a tubal elevation; the tubes connect to the middle ear, equalize pressure and drain middle-ear secretions. During swallowing the soft palate muscles close the choanae and the epiglottis moves anteriorly to close the laryngeal inlet; air passes through the nasal and oral parts into the laryngeal pharynx, then into the trachea.
На 4–5-й неделях беременности по обе сто: Between weeks 4 and 5 of gestation the pharyngeal (branchial) apparatus forms on each side of the developing pharynx, consisting of arches, pouches, clefts and membranes, and the entire pharynx develops from it. Pharyngeal musculature comes from the third, fourth and sixth arches: the third arch gives rise to the stylopharyngeus and the fourth and sixth arches give rise to the constrictor and longitudinal muscle groups; each arch's neurovascular bundle also supplies branches to that arch's muscles.
Артериальное кровоснабжение — из наружно: Arterial supply comes from the external carotid artery through four branches: the ascending pharyngeal, tonsillar (a branch of the facial artery), maxillary and lingual arteries; pharyngeal veins drain into the internal jugular vein.
Лимфоотток: прямой — непосредственно в г: Lymphatic drainage is direct, straight to the deep cervical lymph nodes along the internal jugular vein, or indirect, through retropharyngeal or paratracheal nodes before reaching the deep cervical nodes. The Waldeyer ring is a ring of lymphoid tissue guarding the entrances to the GI and respiratory tracts: superiorly the pharyngeal tonsils (adenoids) in the roof of the nasopharynx; laterally the palatine tonsils and tubal tonsils (around the auditory tubes); inferiorly the lingual tonsils on the posterior tongue.
Чувствительная иннервация слизистой всех: Sensory (afferent) supply to the mucosa of all three regions, carrying pain, temperature, pressure and touch: nasopharynx, the maxillary division of the trigeminal nerve (CN V2); oropharynx, the glossopharyngeal nerve (CN IX); laryngopharynx, the internal laryngeal nerve, a branch of the superior laryngeal nerve (vagus, CN X). Motor (efferent) supply is by CN IX and CN X: the stylopharyngeus is the only pharyngeal muscle supplied by CN IX, and the vagus supplies all other pharyngeal muscles.
Четыре констриктора и три продольные мыш: There are four constrictors and three longitudinal muscles. Superior constrictor: origin on the medial pterygoid plate, pterygoid hamulus, pterygomandibular ligament and mylohyoid line of the mandible; insertion on the pharyngeal tubercle of the occipital bone and the posterior pharyngeal raphe; it helps close the soft palate during swallowing and propels the bolus downward. Middle constrictor: origin on the inferior stylohyoid ligament and the lesser and greater horns (cornua) of the hyoid, insertion on the pharyngeal raphe; it propels the bolus downward. Inferior constrictor: origin on the thyroid cartilage lamina and cricoid cartilage, insertion on the pharyngeal raphe; it propels the bolus downward. Cricopharyngeus: the lowest fibers of the inferior constrictor, which acts as a sphincter at the inferior end of the pharynx and helps prevent reflux of esophageal contents.
Продольные мышцы: шилоглоточная — от шил: Longitudinal muscles: the stylopharyngeus (origin on the styloid process of the temporal bone, insertion on the posterior thyroid cartilage) elevates the pharynx during swallowing; the palatopharyngeus (origin on the palatine aponeurosis, insertion on the posterior thyroid cartilage) elevates the pharynx, pulls the palatopharyngeal arches medially and propels the bolus during swallowing; the salpingopharyngeus (origin on the auditory tube, merging with the palatopharyngeus) with the two muscles above elevates the pharynx during swallowing.
В продольных мышцах возможны небольшие в: Minor variants may exist in the longitudinal muscles, including extra insertions into the palatine tonsils and laryngeal cartilages (epiglottis, arytenoid and thyroid); the salpingopharyngeus is present in only 63% of cadavers, and most of those lacking it were thin individuals.
Операции на глотке требуют аккуратной те: Pharyngeal surgery requires careful technique because of the overlying neurovascular structures and muscles; key surgical concerns are breathing problems, dysphagia and malignancy resection, breathing and swallowing assessment is critical after surgery and feeding tubes are an important alternative route for nutrition. In lateral pharyngoplasty for obstructive sleep apnea the stylopharyngeus should be preserved. Airway management options include endotracheal intubation, which bypasses the pharynx, devices, and cricothyroidotomy as a life-saving option if other methods fail; tonsillar enlargement and neck trauma can compromise the airway.
Фарингит (боль в горле): чаще всего вызы: Pharyngitis (sore throat) is most commonly caused by viruses, with discomfort, pain, irritation and dysphagia; pain is treated with NSAIDs in adults and children (aspirin is an additional option for adults), and Streptococcus pyogenes infection requires etiologic diagnosis and specific treatment. Dysphagia is difficulty swallowing due to muscle weakness, nerve damage or disease, with complications of aspiration of food or saliva and malnutrition; it affects about 50% of elderly patients and 50% of patients with neurological dysfunction. Adenoiditis is inflammation of the adenoids in the upper nasopharynx, usually secondary to infection, with cold-like symptoms, rhinorrhea, nasal obstruction and breathing problems.
Апноэ сна: мышцы глотки могут становитьс: Sleep apnea: pharyngeal muscles can become hypotonic, especially during sleep, and fail to keep the airway open, with associated factors of obesity, generalized hypotonia and macroglossia. Zenker diverticulum occurs at the Killian dehiscence, a small triangular gap between the inferior constrictor and cricopharyngeus: weakness or hypotonia allows the mucosa and submucosa to herniate and food collects in the pouch, and because it involves only the mucosa and submucosa, not the muscular layer, it is a false diverticulum. Cricopharyngeal achalasia (rare): the cricopharyngeus fails to open adequately, whereas normally the upper esophageal sphincter relaxes during swallowing to let the bolus pass; when the muscle is weak or fails to relax, food can leak, causing discomfort and dysphagia, and failure of the cricopharyngeus to relax can contribute to both dysphagia and Zenker diverticulum.

Nerves, lymphatic vessels and the pericardium are not represented in BodyParts3D. The heart is shown as context.
Средостение — пространство вдоль грудной: The thoracic mediastinum is the compartment running the length of the thoracic cavity, between the lungs' pleural sacs, from the thoracic inlet to the superior surface of the diaphragm. There are no physical barriers between compartments other than the pericardium, so it is discussed by subdivision; the four-compartment model divides it into superior, anterior, middle and posterior portions. It houses the heart, great vessels, trachea and essential nerves and serves as a protected pathway between the neck and abdomen.
Верхнее: сверху — верхняя апертура грудн: Superior: the thoracic outlet (superior), the transverse thoracic plane (plane of Ludwig) or sternal angle (inferior), the medial pleural sacs (lateral), the sternum (anterior) and the first four thoracic vertebral bodies (posterior). Anterior: the pericardium (posterior), medial pleural sacs (lateral), and the sternum, transversus thoracis and left 5th to 7th costal cartilages (anterior). Middle: the pericardial sac (anterior and posterior), reflected to the medial pleural sacs (bilateral), the transverse thoracic plane (superior) and the thoracic surface of the diaphragm (inferior). Posterior: the pericardium (anterior), the thoracic diaphragm surface (inferior), the transverse thoracic plane (superior), bodies of T5 to T12 (posterior) and the pleural sacs (lateral).
Верхнее: тимус, трахея, пищевод; дуга ао: Superior: the thymus, trachea and esophagus; the aortic arch, brachiocephalic trunk, left common carotid and left subclavian artery; the superior vena cava, brachiocephalic veins, arch of the azygos and thoracic duct; the left and right vagus, recurrent laryngeal, cardiac, and left and right phrenic nerves; its function is as a conduit for structures passing between head, neck and thorax. Anterior: the thymus, internal thoracic branches (arteries and veins) and parasternal lymph nodes, with no nerves listed; its function is protective, with fatty and connective tissue cushioning the thymus and the cardiac structures behind it.
Среднее: сердце и корни крупных сосудов,: Middle: the heart and great vessel roots, trachea and main bronchi; the ascending aorta, pulmonary trunk and pericardiacophrenic arteries; the superior vena cava, pulmonary veins and pericardiacophrenic veins; the phrenic, vagus and sympathetic nerves; its function is to house the heart and great vessel roots. Posterior: the esophagus; the descending thoracic aorta; the azygos and hemiazygos veins and thoracic duct; the vagus, splanchnic and sympathetic chain; its function is as a conduit between the thoracic and abdominal cavities, described as a continuation of the superior mediastinum.
В средостении расположены сердце и крупн: The mediastinum holds the heart and great vessels, so many vessels pass through it, and lymphatics are also abundant because they closely integrate with the cardiovascular system. Superior: the aortic arch and its three branches (brachiocephalic trunk, left common carotid, left subclavian), with smaller branches being thymic branches of the internal thoracic arteries, proximal pericardiacophrenic arteries and the 3rd and 4th posterior intercostal arteries; most lymphatic drainage collects in the thoracic duct, which empties at the left subclavian vein. Anterior: the internal thoracic arteries descend deep to the lateral sternal borders, then branch into musculophrenic and superior epigastric arteries; lymphatics are the parasternal, pericardial and superior diaphragmatic nodes.
Среднее: коронарные артерии и их ветви;: Middle: the coronary arteries and branches; pericardial lymphatics form a dense network penetrating all cardiac layers and drain posteriorly to pretracheal nodes between the aorta and trachea. Posterior: the descending aorta runs slightly left of midline toward the diaphragm, with notable branches being the proximal intercostal arteries; lymphatics are the thoracic duct and the retrocardiac, diaphragmatic, posterior mediastinal and prevertebral nodes.
Верхнее: нервы, пришедшие сверху — левый: Superior: nerves from above the thorax are the left and right phrenic nerves (C3 to C5), left and right vagus nerves, esophageal plexus, inferior cervical and thoracic cardiac branches and recurrent laryngeal nerves; nerves originating within the thorax are the superior portion of the sympathetic trunk (T1 to T4) and its thoracic cardiac and pulmonary branches. Anterior: no major named nerves. Middle: dense autonomic innervation, sympathetic from sympathetic trunk branches around T2 to T4 and parasympathetic from left and right vagus branches, with somatic innervation from phrenic nerve branches to the fibrous and parietal pericardial layers; because the middle mediastinum is bounded by the pericardium, only a small portion of these nerves actually lie within it. Posterior: sympathetic nerves from the sympathetic chain at T5 to T12, parasympathetic from the left and right vagus nerves, which form the esophageal plexus, and somatic intercostal nerves.
Верхнее: скелетная и гладкая мускулатура: Superior: esophageal skeletal and smooth muscle and the left and right inferior oblique portions of the longus colli, which help mobilize the cervical spine. Anterior: the transversus thoracis, an accessory muscle of expiration, which originates on the posterolateral sternum and helps depress the ribs during active expiration. Middle: the heart. Posterior: the distal smooth muscular portion of the esophagus. Many large mediastinal vessels have multiple layers of smooth muscle supporting cardiovascular homeostasis.
Организация отделов мало различается меж: Compartment organization varies little between individuals, but the structures within each compartment are highly variable. Superior: an absent brachiocephalic trunk (the right common carotid and right subclavian arise directly from the arch), patent ductus arteriosus and tracheoesophageal fistula. Anterior: pectus excavatum, thymic aplasia and thymic cyst. Middle: dextrocardia, heart side dominance (determined by which coronary artery gives rise to the posterior interventricular branch), patent foramen ovale, tetralogy of Fallot and ventricular septal defects. Posterior: bronchogenic cysts, esophageal atresia and esophageal stenosis.
Верхнее: проникающие ранения с высокой в: Superior: penetrating wounds have a high likelihood of injuring major vessels or nerves, causing critical damage on impact and during extraction; the aortic arch, a potential aneurysm site, carries the entire cardiac output, and an untreated arch aneurysm can dissect and cause near-instant death; the esophagus and trachea here are commonly obstructed or injured by ingested or inhaled foreign substances. Anterior: the thymus is involved in myasthenia gravis, pure red cell aplasia and thymic cancer, and its location directly behind the sternum makes it vulnerable to anterior chest trauma, which can cause intrathoracic or thymic hematoma.
Среднее часто считают самым важным отдел: Middle: often considered the most important subdivision, as it contains the pericardium, heart and great vessel roots, with conditions including myocardial infarction, pericardial effusion, cardiac tamponade, tetralogy of Fallot and cardiomegaly. Posterior: clinical importance comes largely from structures descending from the superior mediastinum (descending aorta, autonomic networks, lymphatics and esophagus); descending thoracic aortic aneurysm, thoracic duct obstruction and distal esophageal dysphagia can quickly become life-threatening. Overall, the mediastinum is involved in acute and chronic, infectious and traumatic, and congenital and neoplastic disease, so understanding its anatomy is essential to clinicians at all levels.
Показаны наружные, внутренние и самые вн: The model shows the external, internal and innermost intercostal muscles, the diaphragm, serratus anterior, pectoralis minor, the posterior serratus muscles, levatores costarum and sternocleidomastoid. The subclavius, transversus thoracis, subcostal and scalene muscles are not in BodyParts3D.
Грудную стенку образуют пять групп мышц:: The thoracic wall consists of five muscle groups: external intercostals, internal intercostals, innermost intercostals, subcostals and transversus thoracis, which mainly change the volume of the thoracic cavity during breathing. Muscles attached to but not forming the wall are, anteriorly, the pectoralis major, pectoralis minor, subclavius and serratus anterior, and posteriorly the levatores costarum, serratus posterior superior and serratus posterior inferior; anterior thoracic muscles move the upper extremity and shoulder, while posterior muscles help change thoracic volume and reinforce the wall.
Диафрагма — главная мышца вдоха: она обр: The diaphragm is the primary muscle of inspiration, forms the thoracic floor and separates thoracic and abdominal contents; the scalene and sternocleidomastoid muscles are accessory muscles that give limited help with breathing.
Одиннадцать пар межрёберных мышц лежат в: Eleven pairs of intercostal muscles occupy the intercostal spaces, arranged superficial to deep. The external intercostals (most superficial) run from the rib above to the rib below in an inferomedial direction, from the rib tubercle posteriorly to the costochondral junction anteriorly, where they become the external intercostal membranes; they contract on inspiration, lifting the lateral ribs and widening the thorax transversely. The internal intercostals (middle layer) run perpendicular to the externals, from the costal groove of the rib above to the rib below, from the sternum anteriorly to the rib angles posteriorly, where they become the internal intercostal membranes; they depress the ribs and reduce thoracic volume in forced expiration. The innermost intercostals (deepest layer) attach from the medial costal groove of the rib above to the inner surface of the rib below; endothoracic fascia lines them and lies just superficial to the parietal pleura, and they are thought to assist the internal intercostals in forced expiration.
Подрёберные мышцы лежат в том же слое, ч: The subcostal muscles lie in the same layer as the innermost intercostals and are most abundant in the lower posterior wall, arising from the inner surface of a lower rib and inserting on the inner surface of the second or third rib below. The transversus thoracis is also in the innermost layer, arising from the posterior lower sternum, crossing the inner thoracic cage and inserting on ribs 2 to 6; the subcostals and transversus thoracis both depress ribs in forced expiration.
Задние мышцы грудной клетки, возможно по: Posterior thoracic muscles that may aid respiration: the levatores costarum (from the transverse processes of C7 to T11 to the rib below), which provide limited inspiratory help by elevating ribs; the serratus posterior superior (ribs 2 to 5), which elevates them on inspiration; and the serratus posterior inferior (connecting vertebrae to ribs 8 to 12), which depresses them in forced expiration.
Диафрагма прикрепляется к мечевидному от: The diaphragm attaches to the xiphoid process (sternal part), the costal margin and lower 6 ribs (costal part) and the lumbar vertebrae (lumbar part). On contraction the central tendon moves inferiorly and the dome flattens, increasing the vertical thoracic diameter and lowering intrathoracic pressure, which draws air in; relaxation and elevation during expiration allow air to be expelled. It also raises intra-abdominal pressure during micturition, defecation and weightlifting.
Другие вспомогательные мышцы вдоха: лест: Other inspiratory aids: the scalenes elevate ribs 1 and 2 and the sternocleidomastoid helps elevate the sternum. Anterior muscles acting on the upper limb: the pectoralis major (from the medial clavicle, anterior sternum, first 7 costal cartilages and external oblique aponeurosis to the lateral lip of the intertubercular sulcus of the humerus; flexes, adducts and medially rotates the arm); the pectoralis minor (from ribs 3 to 5 and the overlying intercostal fascia to the coracoid process; depresses the shoulder, protracts the scapula and can elevate ribs 3 to 5 to assist inspiration); the subclavius (from the costochondral junction of rib 1 to the subclavian groove of the clavicle; stabilizes the clavicle); and the serratus anterior (from the superolateral surfaces of ribs 1 to 8 or 1 to 9 to the superior angle, medial border and inferior angle of the scapula; protracts and rotates the scapula, the "boxer's muscle," and can elevate ribs when the shoulder girdle is fixed).
Скелетные мышцы развиваются из мезодермы: Skeletal muscle develops from mesoderm: between weeks 4 and 8 paraxial mesoderm forms paired somites beside the neural tube, each somite splits into the dorsolateral dermomyotome and the ventromedial sclerotome, the dermomyotome gives rise to thoracic skeletal muscle and dermis, and the sclerotome forms the axial skeleton.
Межрёберные артерии снабжают большую час: Intercostal arteries supply most of the thoracic wall and posterior thoracic muscles; each space has 3 arteries (1 posterior, 2 anterior) running between the internal and innermost intercostals in the costal groove, anastomosing laterally. The posterior arteries of spaces 1 and 2 come from the supreme intercostal artery (costocervical trunk of the subclavian); the posterior arteries of spaces 3 to 11, plus a pair of subcostal arteries, arise directly from the descending thoracic aorta, and veins drain to the azygos or hemiazygos systems. The anterior arteries of spaces 1 to 6 are branches of the internal thoracic artery (from the subclavian's first part) and those of spaces 7 to 9 come from the musculophrenic artery (terminal branch of the internal thoracic), with veins draining to the internal thoracic or musculophrenic veins.
Лимфатические сосуды стенки — окологруди: Thoracic wall lymphatics are the parasternal and intercostal nodes: the upper parasternal and upper intercostal nodes drain to the bronchomediastinal trunk and the lower intercostal nodes to the thoracic duct. Anterior muscles: the pectoralis major and minor are supplied by the pectoral branch of the thoracoacromial trunk (second branch of the axillary artery) with veins draining via the pectoral vein to the subclavian vein; the subclavius by the clavicular branch of the thoracoacromial trunk; the serratus anterior by the lateral thoracic, superior thoracic and thoracodorsal arteries; superficial thoracic wall lymph typically drains to axillary or parasternal nodes. Diaphragm: arterial supply from the musculophrenic branch of the internal thoracic, superior phrenic branches of the aorta, lower 5 intercostal arteries, subcostal artery and inferior phrenic arteries; its lymphatics drain to mediastinal nodes and ultimately reach the bloodstream via the thoracic duct.

Грудинная мышца (sternalis) — редкая доб: The sternalis muscle is a rare supernumerary anterior chest wall muscle present in about 8% of people, lying vertically between the superficial and pectoral fasciae parallel to the right sternal margin, with an average size of about 7.0 cm long and 2.9 cm wide, unilateral in about 4.5% and bilateral in under 1.7%; it may aid shoulder movement or assist elevation of the lower chest wall, is innervated by the external or internal thoracic nerves in 55%, intercostal nerves in 43% and both in 2%, and its embryologic origin is uncertain, with no directly attributable clinical symptoms reported; it can cause ECG changes or be mistaken for breast masses on mammography and may complicate breast and cardiothoracic surgery if undetected, but if identified preoperatively it can serve as a muscle flap in anterior chest, head and neck, or breast reconstruction.

Needle thoracostomy is emergency decompression, typically for tension pneumothorax, at the 2nd intercostal space at the midclavicular line or the 4th or 5th intercostal space at the anterior axillary line, inserted just above the rib to minimize neurovascular injury. An intercostal nerve block relieves pain from rib fractures or herpes zoster, with the needle near the inferior rib border passing through skin, superficial fascia, serratus anterior, external and internal intercostals to reach the nerve; adjacent intercostal nerves should also be blocked, since collateral branches and dermatome overlap can cause incomplete relief.

Accessory muscle use during strenuous activity (exercise, singing) is normal, while accessory muscle use at rest may signal disease, such as an asthma exacerbation, and needs evaluation. Accessory respiratory muscles are the scalenes, sternocleidomastoid, internal intercostals, transversus thoracis, pectoralis major and minor, serratus anterior, serratus posterior superior and inferior, latissimus dorsi, trapezius and abdominal muscles.

Лёгочная вентиляция (дыхание) — движение: Pulmonary ventilation (breathing) is the movement of air into and out of the lungs: inhalation draws air in and exhalation expels it. Boyle's law applies: at constant temperature, gas pressure falls as volume rises. Enlarging the thoracic cavity lowers intrathoracic pressure, which draws air in; shrinking the cavity, usually by relaxing the inspiratory muscles, raises intrathoracic pressure and produces exhalation. The thoracic wall includes the sternum, 12 rib pairs, 12 thoracic vertebrae and the associated muscles, fascia and skin; it protects the heart, lungs, great vessels and some abdominal organs, and its bones provide muscle attachment points and enable ventilation.
Рёбра — изогнутые плоские кости, прикреп: Ribs are curved, flat bones attached posteriorly to the vertebrae and anteriorly to the sternum. Rib heads have 1 or 2 facets that articulate with the costal facets of the thoracic vertebral bodies: ribs 1, 10, 11 and 12 have a single head facet that articulates only with their own vertebra, while ribs 2 through 9 have two head facets, the superior facet joining the vertebra above and the inferior facet joining the same-numbered vertebra. Ribs 1 through 10 have tubercles that articulate with the costal facet of the transverse process, while ribs 11 and 12 have no tubercle and do not articulate with a transverse process.
Грудина состоит из рукоятки, тела и мече: The sternum has three parts: the manubrium, body and xiphoid process; the manubrium is the widest part and contains the jugular (sternal) and clavicular notches, the sternal angle (angle of Louis) joins the manubrium and body and the second rib attaches here, and the xiphoid process has no rib attachments but provides attachment for the diaphragm and rectus abdominis. Ribs 1–7 are true (vertebrocostal) ribs and attach directly to the sternum; ribs 8–10 are false (vertebrochondral) ribs, each one's cartilage joining the cartilage of the rib above and ending at the seventh rib's sternal attachment; ribs 11 and 12 are floating (vertebral or free) ribs, ending in posterior abdominal musculature without sternal attachment. Costal cartilages of ribs 1–10 provide elastic recoil, contributing to passive exhalation.
Мышцы стенки делятся на инспираторные и: Thoracic wall muscles fall into two groups: inspiratory and forced expiratory. Inhalation increases the anteroposterior, vertical and transverse thoracic dimensions. The dome-shaped diaphragm pulls the central tendon inferiorly on contraction, flattening the dome and increasing the vertical dimension; the external intercostals lift the lateral ribs ("bucket handle" motion), increasing transverse diameter; the vertebrosternal ribs move in a "pump handle" motion that raises the sternum, increasing the anteroposterior dimension. Neck muscles can assist inspiration: the serratus posterior superior elevates ribs 2–5, the scalenes (when the neck is fixed) elevate ribs 1 and 2, the sternocleidomastoid can assist in raising the sternum and the pectoralis minor assists in lifting ribs 3, 4 and 5 when needed.
Форсированный выдох: внутренние межрёбер: For forced exhalation, the internal intercostals lie deep to the external intercostals, run perpendicular to them and depress the ribs; the transversus thoracis spans the inner thoracic cage from the lower posterior sternum to ribs 2–6, aiding rib depression; and the serratus posterior inferior connects the vertebrae to ribs 8–12 and depresses them. Normal exhalation is passive.
Грудная стенка — часть осевого скелета,: The thoracic wall is part of the axial skeleton, formed from paraxial mesoderm; somites divide into the sclerotome (bone), myotome (muscle) and dermatome. Sclerotome-derived elements begin elongating into ribs in the fifth week of gestation, and ossification starts in the fetal period and is not complete until adulthood. The myotome gives rise to the thoracic wall muscles. The sternum forms from paired sternal bars that meet at the midline; sternal fusion begins in the seventh week, proceeds from superior to inferior and is finished by the tenth week.
Кровоснабжение каждого межрёберного пром: Blood supply per intercostal space is one posterior intercostal artery and a pair of anterior intercostal arteries. The posterior arteries of spaces 1 and 2 arise from the superior (supreme) intercostal artery, a branch of the subclavian artery, and the remaining posterior intercostal arteries and a pair of subcostal arteries arise from the thoracic aorta; posterior arteries enter the costal groove near the rib angle, running between the intercostal vein and nerve, and posterior and anterior intercostal arteries anastomose laterally. The internal thoracic artery (a subclavian branch) supplies the anterior intercostal arteries of spaces 1–6, then divides into the superior epigastric and musculophrenic arteries, and the musculophrenic artery supplies the anterior intercostal arteries of spaces 7–9; the two lowest intercostal spaces receive blood only from posterior intercostal arteries and their collaterals and have no anterior intercostal arteries.
Межрёберные вены идут вверх в рёберных б: Intercostal veins run superiorly in the costal grooves, with 11 posterior intercostal veins and one pair of subcostal veins; posterior intercostal veins anastomose with anterior intercostal veins. Several superior posterior veins typically merge into the left and right superior intercostal veins at T3 or T4, draining into the brachiocephalic vein or superior vena cava, while the remaining posterior intercostal veins drain into the azygos vein, then into the superior vena cava; internal thoracic veins accompany the arteries and drain into the brachiocephalic vein. Дыхательный центр продолговатого мозга р: The medullary respiratory center in the medulla oblongata controls ventilation rate and depth: the dorsal respiratory group controls motor neurons for all inspiration, and the ventral respiratory group controls forced exhalation, while normal exhalation is passive. The phrenic nerve arises from the cervical plexus, mostly from C4 with contributions from C3 and C5, and both phrenic nerves pass through the neck and thorax to innervate the diaphragm. Anterior rami of T1–T11 form the intercostal nerves and the anterior ramus of T12 forms the subcostal nerve; part of the T1 anterior ramus contributes to the brachial plexus, while the other intercostal nerves do not form plexuses. Afferent fibers carry sensation, including from overlying skin, and efferent fibers supply motor input to respiratory muscles.
Тело грудины обычно длиннее и толще у му: The sternal body is usually longer and thicker in males and shorter and thinner in females, which can aid sex determination in skeletal remains. Variants include a bifid xiphoid and a bifid sternum; a sternal foramen results from incomplete ossification of the left and right sternal centers and can be mistaken for a penetrating injury on X-ray, and the sternum is noted as a common acupuncture site where injury could occur. Ectopia cordis is a congenital, more severe sternal malformation in which the heart may be exposed through the thoracic wall due to sternal and pericardial maldevelopment.
Раздвоенные рёбра: передняя часть расщеп: Bifid ribs have an anterior portion that splits into two before reaching the sternum, with associated muscles, vessels and nerves also bifurcating, and are usually unilateral and asymptomatic; a cervical rib is elongation of the seventh cervical vertebra's costal element, usually not reaching the sternum, and a lumbar rib is the same anomaly at L1; failure of the 12th rib's costal element to elongate can prevent its development, leaving some people with 11 ribs.
Сосуды и нервы передней грудной стенки п: Vessels and nerves of the anterior thorax run in the costal groove on the inferior aspect of each rib. Needle thoracostomy is a puncture over the superior aspect of the rib on the affected side, with the second intercostal space at the midclavicular line and the fourth and fifth intercostal spaces at the anterior axillary line studied as sites; a chest tube (tube thoracostomy) is placed in the fourth or fifth intercostal space, tracking above the rib, between the midaxillary and anterior axillary lines. In a left thoracotomy the left phrenic nerve runs along the pericardium and should be avoided to reduce the risk of phrenic nerve palsy.
Использование добавочных мышц — привлече: Accessory muscle use means recruiting normally inactive muscles to assist ventilation, normal during exercise or singing but significant when a patient is at rest. Injury to the brain, spinal cord or phrenic nerve can paralyze the diaphragm, requiring artificial ventilation, with injury most commonly at or above C4; poliomyelitis has caused similar symptoms in the past. Injury to one phrenic nerve (hemidiaphragm) causes paradoxical diaphragm motion on the affected side during inhalation.
Пневмоторакс — свободный воздух между па: Pneumothorax is free air between the parietal and visceral pleurae, which may cause atelectasis; causes include a ruptured bleb (internal) or a broken rib or penetrating wound (external), and treatment may involve removing the air by thoracentesis/needle thoracotomy or placing a chest tube. Flail chest is two or more ribs fractured in two or more places, creating a free-moving segment; early on, intercostal muscles may internally splint the segment, but with fatigue it moves paradoxically, which can significantly impair ventilation.

Атлантоосевой сустав — синовиальный одно: The atlantoaxial joint is a synovial joint classified as a uniaxial pivot joint, in the upper neck between C1 (atlas) and C2 (axis); it permits rotation only, around a central bony pivot held in place by craniovertebral ligaments.
Сустав состоит из трёх синовиальных комп: The joint has three synovial components, one median joint and two lateral (bilateral) joints. The median joint is formed by the dens of C2 and two ligamentous structures, the osteoligamentous ring of the atlas anteriorly and the transverse ligament posteriorly; the two lateral joints are classified as gliding joints. C1 and C2 lie at the craniovertebral junction and differ structurally from the rest of the cervical spine, and the joint has no intervertebral disc. An articular capsule surrounds the joint, connecting the margins of the atlas lateral masses to the posterior surface of the axis.
Функции: позволяет поворачивать голову в: Functions: it allows the head to turn left or right (the article cites roughly 600 head and neck movements per hour in humans), stabilizes the head and supports its weight in a neutral position, helps protect the spinal cord from external compression, provides a passage for the vertebral arteries supplying blood to the brain, and works with the neck muscles to facilitate head and neck movement.
Атлант (C1): кольцеобразный; через боков: The atlas (C1) is ring-shaped, articulates with the cranium via its lateral masses and with the axis, has no spinous process or vertebral body, contains the transverse ligament lying between the superior articular facets, and has anterior and posterior arches, the posterior arch forming a groove for the vertebral artery. The axis (C2) has the dens (odontoid process), which projects superiorly from its anterior portion and articulates with the atlas, plus superior articular facets, a bifid spinous process and bilateral transverse foramina.
Клеточные деления в период беременности: Cell divisions during gestation and the first two weeks after fertilization form the blastocyst, and gastrulation at the end of week two produces the ectoderm, mesoderm and endoderm. Mesodermal somites migrate and mature into vertebrae, with ossification beginning at primary ossification centers as the notochord involutes; development steps are gastrulation and somatic mesoderm formation, condensation of mesoderm into somites, dermomyotome and sclerotome reorganization, somite segmentation, and chondrification and ossification.
У осевого позвонка один центр окостенени: The axis has one ossification center for the body, two for the neural arches and one for the dens; dens ossification centers can be mistaken for fractures in children, since the dens-body junction does not fully fuse until about age six. The article states the body and dens fuse by 4 to 6 years and development is complete by age 25.
Сустав снабжают ветви глубокой шейной, з: The atlantoaxial joint receives blood from branches of the deep cervical, occipital and vertebral arteries; the vertebral arteries exit the axis transverse foramen, run slightly laterally to the atlas transverse foramen and enter the cranium, and collateral branches supply the cervical vertebral bodies and the cervical radicular arteries. The vertebral arteries arise from the subclavian arteries, ascend bilaterally and converge to form the basilar artery, which supplies the brainstem. The article does not describe the lymphatics.
Иннервация сустава — главным образом вет: Innervation of the atlantoaxial joint is mainly from branches of the second cervical spinal nerve. Each cervical vertebra has ventral and dorsal nerve roots on each side, which converge in the spinal foramen to form spinal nerves; there are seven cervical vertebrae but eight pairs of cervical spinal nerves, and spinal nerves usually exit above their corresponding vertebra, but C8 exits below the C7 vertebra.
Атлантоосевой сустав — самая подвижная ч: The atlantoaxial joint is the most mobile part of the cervical spine, and its main stabilizers are the transverse and alar ligaments. Muscles of the posterior neck and suboccipital triangle stabilize the cervical vertebrae and joints and enable rotation, flexion/extension and side-bending; the suboccipital group acts as attachments, postural stabilizers and initiators of craniocervical movement and also prevents the occiput from shifting posteriorly on C1. Four suboccipital muscles are named: rectus capitis posterior major and minor, and obliquus capitis superior and inferior.
Краниовертебральные связки, обеспечивающ: Craniovertebral ligaments contributing to stability are the cruciform ligament (transverse ligament of the atlas), the tectorial membrane, the alar ligaments and the apical ligament of the dens.
В отличие от других шейных уровней, межд: Unlike other cervical levels, there is no intervertebral disc between C1 and C2; a bifid spinous process is consistently seen only in C2 to C4, and about 0.3% of the population has a bifid spinous process as low as C7, considered normal variation. The dens or transverse ligament may form incompletely, creating a variant that may predispose to instability and injury.
Os odontoideum — спорный врождённый или: Os odontoideum is a controversial congenital or traumatic dens variant in which a hypoplastic dens has an ossific density at its superior margin, usually seen in children, and it can be orthotopic or dystopic. Persistent ossiculum terminale is a congenital malformation in which secondary ossification centers fail to fuse at the superior edge of the dens, usually stable and found incidentally. Ossification variation is any arrest or partial interruption of bone formation that may disrupt anatomy and function and can cause significant cervical anomalies through growth plate dysfunction.
Переломы зуба: лечение часто срочное. Ти: Dens fractures: repair is often urgent. Type I is very rare and usually stable and typically needs no surgical fixation; type II is unstable and needs stabilization by external fixation with immobilization or internal fixation, and nonsurgical management carries a risk of nonunion. Nonunion risk factors are age over 50 at injury, dens displacement greater than 6 mm and moderate comminution, and an anterior fixation approach is associated with higher success rates. Halo immobilization carries lower nonunion risk if the patient is under 50 at injury, has minimal dens displacement and no comminution; a halo vest immobilizer provides rigid external support for the upper cervical spine and restricts C1-C2 flexion by 75%.
Атлантоосевая нестабильность без травмы:: Nontraumatic subluxation: ligamentous laxity increases instability risk in spontaneous hyperemic dislocation, nasopharyngeal torticollis (Grisel syndrome), rheumatoid arthritis, trisomy 21, Morquio syndrome and Marfan syndrome, and congenital syndromes may cause incomplete odontoid formation or an underdeveloped transverse ligament. Traumatic rotatory subluxation: elderly patients have more bony degeneration, lower bone density and cartilage loss, which may narrow the joint space and raise the risk of life-threatening injury from distraction or subluxation, while children tend to be more hypermobile, so rotational subluxation from hyperflexion and rotation is seen more often in pediatric patients.
Перелом Джефферсона (перелом атланта) с: Jefferson fracture (atlas fracture) with transverse ligament rupture occurs when intense axial loading affects the anterior and posterior arches, is associated with diving headfirst into shallow water and has three subtypes (posterior arch, burst and lateral mass injuries); the transverse and alar ligaments may tear without an atlas fracture, and it is best evaluated by CT and MRI. Dens fractures: type I is avulsion of the odontoid tip at the alar ligament insertion, type II is a fracture at the base of the odontoid process and type III is a fracture extending into the axis body.
Цервикогенная головная боль — вторичная: Cervicogenic headache is a secondary chronic headache from pathology of the upper cervical joints or atlantooccipital joint, with the main symptom of ipsilateral pain in the pericranial muscles; the C1-C3 nerve roots are thought to be the nociceptive source of pain referred to the occiput, and it must be distinguished from cervical artery dysfunction, intracranial pathology and cervical myelopathy. Occipital neuralgia: the posterior cervical plexus (Cruveilhier's plexus) can be entrapped by muscle fibers, and hypertonic suboccipital, trapezius and splenius capitis muscles can compress nerve fibers from the posterior rami of C1-C3, resulting in inflammation, injury and piercing or throbbing pain in the upper neck and occiput.
Плечевое сплетение — сеть нервов, обеспе: The brachial plexus is a network of nerves that provides motor and sensory innervation to the shoulder, arm and hand; it arises from the ventral rami of C5 through T1, and its structure from proximal to distal is roots, trunks, divisions, cords and terminal branches. Plexus injuries are among the most debilitating upper-extremity injuries, so knowledge of its anatomy and variations is important for diagnosis and treatment.
Корешки — передние ветви C5–T1. Стволы:: Roots are the ventral rami of C5 to T1; trunks are superior (C5-C6), middle (C7) and inferior (C8-T1); each trunk splits into anterior and posterior divisions (six in total); cords are lateral, posterior and medial, named for their position relative to the axillary artery; the five terminal branches are the musculocutaneous, axillary, radial, median and ulnar nerves. Collateral branches arise proximal to the roots, trunks or cords and supply proximal limb muscles.
Передние разделения (мышечно-кожный, сре: The anterior divisions (musculocutaneous, median, ulnar) innervate anterior arm, forearm and intrinsic hand muscles, mainly providing limb flexion; the posterior divisions (axillary, radial) innervate the posterior arm and forearm, enabling elbow, wrist and finger extension.
К пятой неделе внутриутробного развития: By the fifth week in utero, forelimb buds appear as paddle-shaped structures extending from the level of the C4 to T1 somites; peripheral nerves grow from the developing brachial plexus into the limb mesenchyme, and spinal nerves form segmental bands along the dorsal and ventral limb surfaces. Following a proximal-to-distal gradient, proximal muscles are supplied by the higher bands (C5, C6) and distal muscles by the lower bands (C8, T1).
Большая часть сплетения снабжается подкл: Most of the plexus is supplied by the subclavian artery and its branches; the vertebral artery, via anterior and posterior spinal branches, supplies the cervical rootlets; the trunks are supplied by the superior intercostal and deep cervical arteries, or directly by the subclavian artery; and the cords by the subclavian, subscapular and axillary arteries. Lymphatics are not covered in the article.
Мышечно-кожный (C5–C6) иннервирует все п: The musculocutaneous nerve (C5-C6) innervates all anterior arm muscles and provides elbow flexion and supination via biceps brachii. The median nerve (C5-T1) innervates part of the anterior forearm and the thenar and central hand, providing forearm pronation, wrist and digit flexion and thumb opposition. The ulnar nerve (C8-T1) innervates part of the anterior forearm and the hypothenar and central hand, providing adduction of digits 2-5 (palmar), abduction (dorsal) and thumb adduction. The axillary nerve (C5-C6) innervates the deltoid (abduction) and teres minor (external rotation). The radial nerve (C5-T1) innervates the posterior upper arm and forearm, providing extension of wrist, elbow and digit MCP joints and supination via the supinator.
Коллатеральные нервы и их мишени: дорсал: Collateral nerves and their targets: dorsal scapular, the rhomboids; long thoracic, serratus anterior; suprascapular, supraspinatus and infraspinatus; lateral pectoral, pectoralis major; medial pectoral, pectoralis major and minor; upper subscapular, subscapularis; lower subscapular, subscapularis and teres major; thoracodorsal, latissimus dorsi; medial brachial cutaneous, medial arm skin; medial antebrachial cutaneous, medial forearm skin. The long thoracic nerve allows scapular protraction and superior rotation, and the suprascapular nerve allows shoulder abduction (supraspinatus) and lateral rotation (infraspinatus).
Анатомические варианты важны для предотв: Anatomic variations matter for avoiding iatrogenic injury, and surgeons should know them before upper-limb procedures; reported examples are a split median nerve in the forearm of a 35-year-old male cadaver, with an anomalous muscle, rejoining in the distal forearm; a study of fetal cadavers suggesting higher injury risk for variant nerve branches; direct C6 branches to pectoralis minor and latissimus dorsi; deltoid innervation by C6 and C7 roots; the lateral pectoral nerve arising from the posterior division of the upper trunk; and the median nerve lying lateral to the axillary artery.
Травматические повреждения обычно вызыва: Traumatic injuries typically cause loss of sensation and motor power, and often disabling neuropathic pain. Historically, treatment for a flail arm included amputation, shoulder arthrodesis and prosthetic replacement, and advances in peripheral nerve surgery over recent decades have improved long-term outcomes.
Верхний паралич (Эрба — Дюшенна): C5–C6;: Upper lesions (Erb-Duchenne palsy) affect C5-C6 and are caused by forced separation of head and shoulder in birth injury, disc herniation or accidents; axillary and suprascapular nerve loss shows when the arm is medially rotated and adducted, and musculocutaneous loss shows with forearm extension and pronation and loss of sensation from the lateral forearm to the thumb base, the posture being called "waiter's tip." Lower lesions (Klumpke paralysis) affect C8-T1, often from grabbing an object during a fall, forcing the arm above the head, and also from birth injury or thoracic outlet syndrome, with ulnar nerve and intrinsic hand muscle weakness and sensory loss; claw hand and "ape sign" suggest the diagnosis, and Horner syndrome may co-occur.
Повреждения конечных ветвей. Мышечно-кож: Terminal branch injuries. Musculocutaneous: rare, with lateral forearm sensory loss and weak flexion and supination. Axillary: from anterior dislocation or surgical neck humerus fracture, with lateral arm and deltoid sensory changes and weak abduction above 15 degrees. Median: lateral 3.5 digits and lateral palm sensory loss, weak wrist and finger flexion, pronation and thumb opposition, with signs of ape hand, hand of benediction and ulnar wrist deviation; causes are pronator teres syndrome, carpal tunnel and supracondylar humerus fracture. Radial: "Saturday night palsy" mainly affects the axilla and causes wrist drop, weak elbow, wrist and finger extension and sensory loss over the posterior arm, forearm and dorsal hand; causes include axillary compression (crutches, sleeping with arm over a chair) and midshaft humerus fracture. Ulnar: medial 1.5 digits and hypothenar sensory loss, weak wrist flexion, finger abduction and adduction, thumb adduction and finger extension, with signs of claw hand and radial wrist deviation; causes are medial epicondyle fracture, hamate hook fracture and clavicle injury.
Синдром грудного выхода: сдавление нижне: Thoracic outlet syndrome is lower trunk and subclavian vessel compression, from a cervical rib (present in under 1% of people) or a Pancoast tumor, resembling Klumpke palsy with intrinsic hand atrophy plus ischemia, pain and edema of the arm and hand. Winged scapula is a long thoracic nerve lesion (C5-C7), often after axillary node dissection for mastectomy, with impaired serratus anterior function; the arm cannot abduct beyond 100 degrees.

Поясничное сплетение — крупная нервная с: The lumbar plexus is a major nerve network arising mostly from the lumbar spinal cord; "plexus" means a web of nerves, formed just lateral to where T12 to L5 exit via the intervertebral foramina. The plexus is bilateral, and nerves combine across levels to form larger nerves that supply peripheral tissues, mainly the lower extremities. Its primary functions are motor innervation and cutaneous sensation, mainly of the lower extremities, and the superior nerves also contribute to the lower abdomen and pelvis; the plexus supports knee extension, hip flexion and thigh adduction.
Спинной мозг формируется из нервной плас: The spinal cord forms from the neural plate; peripheral nerves derive from neuroepithelial cells, which give rise to neurons, support cells and axons of the peripheral nervous system. Fetal and adult lumbar plexus morphology is similar, and nerve thickness, length and spinal nerve branching remain consistent through development.

Симптомы: обычно односторонняя боль в се: Symptoms are usually unilateral mid-buttock pain radiating down the leg, with paresthesias in an L5 or S1 dermatomal pattern, and weakness and reflex changes are less common; L5 has no reflex and S1 corresponds to the ankle jerk. The Lasègue straight leg raise (supine) is positive if ipsilateral pain occurs between 10 and 60 degrees, with sensitivity of about 90% but low specificity; contralateral leg pain on this test suggests disc herniation and warrants imaging, and MRI is most useful when the compression level is unclear and also assesses soft tissue, discopathy, infection or neoplasm. Urinary retention or perianal dysesthesia suggests cauda equina syndrome, which requires prompt surgical decompression. Most sciatica is managed conservatively with a few days of rest, pain medication and physical therapy, and surgery is considered for significant stenosis or evidence of nerve irritation.

Symptoms are hip pain radiating into the leg, worsened by driving and sitting, and unlike disc herniation it does not cause paralumbar muscle spasm; estimated prevalence is about 16%, and it is postulated to be the most common form of extraspinal sciatica. Ultrasound-guided lidocaine injection can treat it in the emergency department.

Подмышечная артерия — главный артериальн: The axillary artery is the main arterial supply to the upper limb; it continues from the subclavian artery after that vessel emerges beneath the first rib and enters the axilla. It serves as a landmark for nearby structures, especially the brachial plexus, gives off six branches and ends at the lower border of the teres major, where it becomes the brachial artery. Conditions that can affect it include aneurysms, thrombosis, embolism, arteritis, pseudoaneurysms and thoracic outlet syndrome, and traumatic disruption can cause severe bleeding or limb ischemia; it is a key surgical landmark in bypass grafting, shoulder operations and axillary lymph node dissection.

It is divided into three parts by the pectoralis minor: part 1 (proximal to the pectoralis minor) has 1 branch, part 2 (deep to the pectoralis minor) has 2 branches and part 3 (distal to the pectoralis minor) has 3 branches. The axillary vein runs medial to the artery along its full length. In a study of 59 cadavers the average length was 11.22 cm, with each part occupying roughly equal intervals; the surface marking is a line from the midclavicular point to the groove behind the coracobrachialis.

The subscapular trunk is usually the largest branch and runs down the posterior axillary wall, giving rise to the scapular circumflex artery (which passes through the triangular space, supplies the scapular region and anastomoses with the suprascapular artery, forming a collateral route between parts 1 and 3) and the thoracodorsal artery (which supplies the latissimus dorsi). The anterior humeral circumflex is smaller and runs anterior to the humerus; the posterior humeral circumflex is larger, passes through the quadrilateral space, then runs posterior to the humerus alongside the axillary nerve and supplies the deltoid; both humeral circumflex arteries supply the humeral head and shoulder joint and anastomose with each other. Injuries may be repaired with autologous vein grafts or synthetic grafts such as polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE), depending on the cause (aneurysm, blunt trauma or gunshot wound). The artery can be clamped without harming the arm, and in cardiac surgery the right axillary artery is often used for arterial cannulation, particularly in aortic aneurysm or dissection repair.

Presentations are upper limb neurological deficits, ischemic fingers, or radial and ulnar occlusion from embolization. CT angiography is the most effective imaging modality and the gold standard, MR angiography is an alternative when IV contrast is contraindicated and ultrasound is also highly effective; treatment is aneurysmectomy with saphenous vein grafting, with endovascular repair as an alternative.

Its branches include the deep brachial, superior ulnar collateral and inferior ulnar collateral arteries, and it supplies the biceps brachii, triceps brachii and coracobrachialis. Плечевая артерия традиционно — основной: The brachial artery has traditionally been the main upper-extremity vascular access site, by percutaneous or open approach, and enables complex endovascular procedures; brachial artery occlusion after catheterization is a documented, serious complication, and management includes conservative care, surgical thrombo-embolectomy or balloon angioplasty. The artery can be clamped during surgery to reduce bleeding.

Volkmann's ischemic contracture is a permanent wrist flexion contracture caused by ischemia, which can result from brachial artery injury or obstruction, including improper tourniquet or cast use, compartment syndrome or direct trauma.

The common femoral artery (CFA) continues from the external iliac artery after it passes under the inguinal ligament. The femoral artery, vein and nerve lie in the femoral triangle of the anterior thigh just below the inguinal ligament; from medial to lateral the order is femoral vein, CFA, then femoral nerve. The artery and vein share the femoral sheath; the nerve does not.

The CFA is a common site of peripheral arterial disease (PAD) complications such as claudication and critical limb ischemia, and a preferred site for percutaneous catheterization in many endovascular procedures.

Length and diameter vary with height, weight, sex and body surface area; one study reported an average CFA diameter of 6.19 mm ± 1.2 mm.
